chapters.html:
Morning light filtered in thin streaks through the bakery windows as the sun crept across the still-quiet streets. Inside, the air was warm, carrying the scent of freshly baked bread and honey. Mydei had been up long before the sun was up with nothing but the low hum of the refrigerator keeping him company. 

He stood behind the counter, pen tapping absentmindedly against his cheek as he scanned the checklist in front of him. The inventory was done, the dough had been set out proof, and the pastry case had been restocked. A few boxed orders were ready to go as well and neatly lined up in the refrigerated pick-up cake. 

He crossed off another item, letting out a small sigh as he rolled his shoulders back. The day hadn’t even begun, but the inevitable weight of it had already started to seep in. 

It had been about a month since he and Augusta had moved out of the apartment upstairs into their new home with Phainon. Between wedding planning and work, they still had a lot to unpack. Not to mention the upstairs renovations to expand the bakery and still having to deal with customers. Everything had been piling up lately. 

His fingers found their way to the ring on the chain around his neck, toying with the silver band as he reached beneath the counter without thinking. There was still some time before opening, so there was no harm in just looking. He pulled out the thin stack of glossy magazines—just inspiration for the wedding. He’d already marked a couple of pages, but there was still so much to do. Flower arrangements. Table setting. Seating plans. Colour palette. What they were going to wear—

A knock broke through his spiral.

He set the magazine aside, wiping his hands on the nearest washcloth before stepping out from behind the counter. Phainon stood on the other side of the door, crouching down to peer in through the glass and give Mydei a small wave. 

Mydei smiled despite himself, unlocking the door and pulling it open. 

“What are you doing here?” he asked, smiling just a little wider now. 

Phainon didn’t answer right away. He stepped inside, one hand lifting to tilt Mydei’s chin up with two fingers, just enough so he could lean in to press their lips together in a gentle kiss. Mydei’s eyes fluttered closed, a satisfied hum slipping from him before he could stop it. 

“Had some time before work,” Phainon murmured when he pulled back, still close enough that their breaths mingled. “Thought I’d come see my ever busy fiancé. Holding up okay?”

Mydei let out a breath before heading back toward the counter. “Could use some coffee. You?”

“Please,” Phainon said easily, following just behind him. "I'm going to be dealing with students all day."

Mydei slipped behind the counter, tightening his apron before switching on the espresso machine. The coffee grinder kicked on, filling the space with noise. He grabbed one mug for himself, and one to-go cup for Phainon since he knew he’d have to leave for work soon. Phainon leaned over the counter on his elbows with soft eyes. 

“You’re staring.”

“I know,” Phainon shrugged, the corner of his mouth twitched. 

Mydei playfully rolled his eyes, throwing a glance over his shoulder. “Latte?”

“Mm. Yeah,” Phainon responded thoughtfully. 

Mydei nodded. He pulled the shot of espresso unceremoniously, topping it up with just enough milk before sliding it over to Phainon. “How was Augusta this morning?” he asked. 

Phainon let out a huff of laughter, a little fond. “She barely needed me. She got dressed on her own, and packed her bag. Well—mostly.”

“Mostly?”

“She forgot the field trip form you signed last night, but I put it in her zippy,” he said. “She didn’t even argue about breakfast.”

Mydei stilled. “And she didn’t ask for anything?”

Phainon shook his head. 

“She really is growing up.”

Phainon’s gaze dropped briefly, then he looked up at Mydei again. “...Yeah.”

A beat of silence washed over them. Mydei reached under the counter again for one of the magazines again, flipping to some of the pages he marked. 

“You’ve really been thinking about it.”

“Someone has to,” Mydei said with a pointed look. 

Phainon pouted, bottom lip jutting out in the way that reminded him of their daughter. “I’ve helped.”

“Choosing to have tiramisu instead of a wedding cake hardly counts as helping,” Mydei shot back. 

“It’s creamy and delicious just like—”

“Don’t finish that sentence.”

“You’re the one who said we get three vetoes each and you’ve,” Phainon pointed an accusing finger at him, “vetoed all of my ideas.”

“You get three, not me. Because of your lack of taste. If you have any useful ideas, I could do with those.” 

Phainon paused for a moment. Then, he tilted his head. “It was a perfectly fine choice.”

“Phainon, I love you, but we are not getting married in a sea of purple and yellow.”

Phainon tried to hold his ground for a moment, but it was a futile attempt. He let out a small laugh under his breath. He moved with ease behind the counter, wrapping his arms around Mydei’s waist from behind. 

“Alright. You win. Colour palette is all yours,” he said, chin coming to rest on Mydei’s shoulder. 

Mydei leaned back into him instinctively, bringing one hand up to pat his cheek. Phainon caught his wrist, pressing a kissing into his palm. 

“You know,” he started casually, “If we’re thinking about adding things…”

“No.”

“I didn’t even say anything yet!”

“You didn’t have to.”

“Another baby wouldn’t be so bad, would it?”

Mydei glanced back at him with an unimpressed look. “You just want to see me pregnant.”

Phainon didn’t hesitate. “Well. Yes—I thought that was obvious,” he responded. Quite shameless at that too. 

Mydei narrowed his eyes at him for a second before shaking his head, the movement softened with just enough fondness. “You’re unbelievable.”

“You’d look beauti—”

“Aht,” Mydei pulled his hand away, but his expression flickered for a moment. He considered letting the words slip, but decided against it. Instead, he nudged Phainon with his elbow. “We have the wedding to focus on. And unpacking all our boxes. And the renovations.”

Phainon exhaled, shifting his weight slightly. “You take on too much.”

“Someone has to make sure things get done.” 

“Maybe if you’d let me help…” Phainon began, but Mydei just shook his head. Phainon opened his mouth to say something, probably to argue, but made the correct decision and decided against it. His eyes flickered to the chain around Mydei’s neck. 

“Hey…” his voice was softer this time 

“Hm?”

“Are you going to take my last name?”

Mydei paused for a moment. This wasn’t the first time Phainon had asked. 

“I said I’d think about it,” he replied after a moment. 

“You’ve been saying that for the last three months.”

Mydei pulled away from him gently. 

“You’re going to be late,” he said simply, glancing over at the clock above the refrigerator. 

“Hey–”

Mydei stepped forward, closing the gap between them with a firm kiss to his lips. He brought his hand up to Phainon’s jaw as Phainon’s fingers dug into the fabric of his apron. 

When they pulled apart, Phainon let out a small huff and adjusted his coat. “I know you’re trying to distract me?

“Is it working?” Mydei questioned with a slight smirk tugging at his lips. He moved quickly to grab a neatly wrapped box from the fridge. 

“Lunch. I thought I’d bring it by later, but since you’re here now…” he trailed off, holding out the box for him. 

“Does this mean I won’t see you during lunch hour?”

“You’ll see me at home,” Mydei murmured, a faint streak of pink creeping across his cheeks. Phainon took the box from his hands, reaching out to tuck a loose strand of hair behind his ear. 

“Just… think about it, okay?”

By the time evening settled in, the bakery had finally gone quiet. 

The last of the customers had trickled out, and half the display case had been emptied out. Upstairs, the sound of light drilling and muffled conversation drifted down from the half-finished lounge. 

Mydei stood behind the counter again, sleeves pushed up, sorting through receipts and invoices. A pen rested between his fingers, tapping occasionally against the paper. 

Across from him, Cipher had made herself entirely comfortable, leaned back in one of the chairs with Castorice sitting beside her, a little more observant. 

Augusta was sitting at a small table nearby as she coloured on a piece of paper. She’d been with him since he’d picked her up after school, and after about an hour of taking orders, she’d resigned to playing instead. He couldn’t blame her. 

“Soooo,” Cipher drawled out, eyeing the scattered papers. “You’ve been busy.”

Mydei didn’t look up. “That tends to happen when you run a business.”

“And plan a wedding,” Castorice added. “Have you made any new decisions?”

“Mm.”

“Oh?” she asked. “And?”

Mydei reached for a small piece of cardboard with colour swatches. “We’re going with maroon, blush, and ivory with gold accents.”

Cipher leaned over, scanning it, lips pursed. 

Castorice clapped her hands together. “It’s beautiful.”

“I see you’re not going with purple and yellow,” Cipher snickered. 

Mydei shot her an unimpressed look. 

“You’re welcome to not come.”

“Hey! I didn’t say all that… I like it. It suits you.”

Mydei hummed, satisfied enough with the answer as he wiped down the counter once more. Cipher tilted her head, watching him for a moment. Then, casually, like she hadn’t planned it at all:

“You know,” she said, “Mydei Khaslana has a nice ring to it.”

Mydei paused. 

“....What did my husband-to-be bribe you with?”

Cipher gasped, hand flying dramatically to her chest. “Excuse me? I would never sully my pride by accepting a bribe.”

Mydei wasn’t having it. 

“I’m serious,” she insisted.

“Mm.”

“It’s insulting what you think of me.” She turned to Castorice. “Can you believe this? The disrespect the little prince has.”

Castorice shook her head fondly. “Phainon said she’d be allowed to babysit Augusta again for one night.”

That got the little girl’s attention. Her head snapped toward them. “Really?” she exclaimed, eyes widening. 

“No.”

Augusta frowned, but turned back to her paper just as quickly. 

Cipher groaned, slumping dramatically against the counter like she’d been wounded. “In case you’ve forgotten, you’re my wife,” she said to Castorice before narrowing her eyes at Mydei. “I volunteer my precious time to take care of your child, and yet, you reject my kindness time and time again. It’s a mutually beneficial agreement.”

“You’re a bad influence.”

“I teach her very valuable life skills. She has to get by somehow.”

Mydei shook his head, leaning on his elbows over the counter. “How do you put up with this?”

Castorice hid a small smile behind her hand. “You’re really asking when you have Phainon?”

Mydei considered it for a moment. “Fair enough,” he admitted.

His gaze flicked briefly toward the stairs. Phainon was still up there, overseeing the renovation, but it wouldn’t be long until the crew had to head home.

“...Speaking of which, did he…mention anything else?” he asked.

Cipher raised an eyebrow. “Like what?”

Castorice tilted her head. “No?”

Mydei hesitated for half a second. 

“...About another baby.”

“Oh?” Cipher leaned forward, suddenly invested. 

“Are you… considering it?” Castorice asked. 

“I–” Mydei began, but he stopped him when he heard the sound of footsteps. 

The three of them turned at the same time as Phainon came down the stairs, his hair slightly out of place from running his hands through it one too many times. 

He paused just short of the last step. 

“...What?” 

Cipher’s grin spread. “Oh nothing~ just hearing that the deliverer boy wants this one to deliver something else.”

Phainon’s brows knit together. “What are you talking about?”

“Your new fixation,” Mydei responded. 

“Wanting a baby? Is that… new?” Phainon blinked. 

Castorice cleared her throat, “Should we be here?”

“Unclear,” Cipher whispered, finding all this a little too entertaining. She rested her chin in her hands. “So… how long have you been wanting to knock up the little prince?”

Mydei pinched the bridge of his nose, throwing a quick glance over at Augusta to make sure she hadn’t heard that. She was still colouring, thankfully oblivious to the ongoing conversation. 

“There is something wrong with you,” he muttered.

“Oh please,” Cipher waved him off without a second thought. “I helped you two get back together. Now start talking.”

Phainon opened his mouth to speak, but closed it just as quickly when Mydei shot him a look. 

“...It’s complicated,” he settled on instead.

“Uh-huh,” Cipher nodded thoughtfully. “So since you two got back together.”

Castorice stood first, smoothing down her skirt and adjusting her bag. “Alright, I think it’s time we take our leave.”

Cipher frowned. “Aw come on princess–”

“Now,” Cas said. 

Cipher sighed dramatically but pushed herself up anyway. “Fine. But this conversation is not over,” she added, pointing between them before heading for the door. 

The bell chimed softly as they left. 

Phainon let out a breath, rubbing the back of his neck before glancing toward Augusta. “...Alright babygirl,” he murmured, voice soft. 

He crossed the room and crouched down in front of her. “Hey,” he said, nudging her lightly. “Time to head out.”

Augusta shook her head immediately. “Nooo,” she whined, still clutching a marker. “I’m making a wedding invitation.”

“Oh?” Phainon asked, peering over her shoulder to get a good look at it. “Mama and I might have to print more of these,” he added, reaching out to gently tickle her stomach. She giggled, squirming a little in her chair. “Someone’s getting sleepy, huh?” he teased. 

“I’m not!” she insisted between giggles, but she was already starting to lean toward him. Phainon slipped his hands under her arms and lifted her easily, settling her against his hip. Mydei watched fondly as she wrapped her around his neck, resting her head against his shoulder. 

“Mm,” he hummed. “That’s what I thought.”

Augusta huffed but didn’t argue, her little eyes already fluttering closed. Phainon adjusted his  hold on her before looking over at Mydei and outstretching a hand toward him. 

Mydei grabbed his coat, slipping it on before tucking himself in the space between Phainon’s arm and hip. 

“Yes,” he let out the word, barely a whisper. 

“Hm?”

Mydei turned to face him, eyes softening, a gentle smile gracing his lips.

“I’ll take your last name.”

The house had finally started feeling more like a home. 

The boxes were gone, or at least neatly tucked away so they weren’t tripping over them every morning. Most of the decisions for the wedding had been finalized. The invitations had been sent out, and everything was starting to feel more real. 

And for once, the day had ended without much fuss. Augusta had gone to sleep early after tiring herself out at the park with Phainon, and now their home had settled into the quiet. 

Mydei sat against the headboard, hair still slightly damp from his shower as he scrolled through some unread messages about final wrap-up for the upcoming wedding. Castorice wanted to confirm a few vendors, and since Mydei had decided not to take on the extra task of making their dessert, he still needed to sort out those details too. And... there was still the matter of vows...

Phainon had made himself comfortable on top of Mydei earlier. He was half draped across him, one hand wrapped around his waist like he absolutely had no intention of ever letting go—and knowing him, he probably didn’t. He shifted slightly, nuzzling into Mydei’s chest in the way that always made him roll his eyes. Mydei threaded his fingers through his hair absently as Phainon hummed contently. 

Phainon lifted his head, chin resting on Mydei's chest before plucking his phone from his hands and tossing it off to the side. 

“Phai–”

“Mm-mm," he shook his head. "No working in bed. I barely see you as is, and you're focused on messages?"

"It's things for our wedding," Mydei murmured. 

Phainon let out a deep sigh, pulling Mydei to lay next to him. He planted one hand by the side of his head, turning so he was hovering over him. The other hand came up to cup Mydei's cheek, his ring glinting softly under the lamp light. "And it'll all get done, just let Cas handle it. There's only a couple more weeks to go."

"I don't know..."

"You can tell me if there's something bothering you, you know," Phainon added softly. He leaned down just enough to let their noses brush before firmly pressing his lips against Mydei's. "Something on your mind?"

Mydei averted his gaze. There was so much he'd taken control over for the wedding, and Phainon had been good to him throughout everything. But it was... Phainon's day too, and the thought of imposing yet another request on him seemed like…too much.

"Mydei."

"It's stupid."

"Hey," Phainon said gently. "Just tell me what it is, and then…” he shifted closer, “if it really is stupid then we'll laugh it off together.”

"You're not going to let this go, are you?"

"Not a chance," he punctuated the words with a kiss to the corner of Mydei's mouth. 

Mydei took a breath. "I..." he swallowed the words. "I don't want to do vows."

Phainon's smile fell just as fast as guilt coiled in Mydei's stomach. 

"No…not like that. I didn't mean entirely. It's just... I'm not the best with words, and I know you're better at saying those kinds of things out loud, and I know you've had yours prepared for a while now, and…” Mydei let out a frustrated sigh. “This is coming out all wrong," he admitted.

“I'm not ashamed to say that I love you, but every time I pick up that pen, I can't help but think that everything that I'm thinking are things I should be saying to you. Just you.”

Phainon didn't respond at first, but his posture did change. He moved back from Mydei, guiding him just enough so they were seated cross-legged across from each other. 

"But I've been deciding so much and it's your day too, so–" Mydei started. 

Phainon placed a finger against his lips. 

"Take my hands."

Mydei gave him a questioning look before resting his hands in Phainon's palms reluctantly. 

"What are we doing?"

"Saying our vows," Phainon stated like it was the most obvious thing in the world. 

Mydei chuckled. "We're not even dressed."

Phainon just leaned over, nipping softly at the skin of Mydei's neck, just beneath his jaw. Mydei's eyes fluttered closed instinctively, relishing in the feeling. "Perfect timing then," he responded before pulling back. 

"This is ridiculous."

"Come on, sit properly," Phainon insisted, taking his hands again. "This is officially part of our wedding now."

"Is it?"

"Mhm, I'll go first, okay?" 

Mydei nodded, deciding that he could entertain his antics tonight. 

Phainon's expression instantly softened, eyes shining faintly in the low light of their bedroom. "When I proposed to you, no-even before that, I promised myself that I would love every version of our life. no matter what happened, no matter what secrets were kept, in sickness and in health, and through all that we've lived through together and whatever is to come."

Mydei swallowed, slightly caught off guard by the sincerity in his voice. 

"And I vowed," Phainon continued, thumb brushing over the ring that was now on Mydei's knuckles instead of looped through the chain around his neck. "To never let you forget how much I want you. How I'd choose in every lifetime. Every morning. Every night. And all the little moments in between even if we had to do it over thirty six million, five-hundred fifty thousand, three hundred and thirty six times."

"Really? Where'd you get that number from?" Mydei snorted. 

"Shh.. this is serious. Let me finish," Phainon said a little more insistently. He let out a shaky breath before continuing. "I swore to build a home with you. One we could call our own. A space for the three of us and maybe... more. A place that we could fill up with enough love that none of us would ever feel alone again."

Mydei averted his gaze, throat already feeling tight. Phainon lifted one hand, brushing the back of it against Mydei's cheek. "I mean it every time I say I love you, and I think I fall just a little more with each passing day." 

Mydei's lashes fluttered as he looked away, trying to hide the tears filling his waterline. "You can't just say things like that," he mumbled. 

Phainon chuckled. "Maybe, but hey, you’re the one who started this."

Mydei's response was a squeeze to his hands. He leaned forward, forehead against Phainon's for a moment. 

Phainon pulled back just enough to look at him. 

"Your turn."

"My what?"

"This is a two way street."

"Phai–I didn't–" Mydei's voice faltered. "They're not going to be poetic."

"So? It's just me here," he said gently. “Now come on, sing my praises and tell me how much you love me

That wasn’t the wording Mydei would use. He groaned and rubbed a hand down his face. He straightened his posture, resting his hands in Phainon's once again, a blush already creeping up the back of his neck. 

"Fine," he muttered. "But if I sound stupid, it's your fault."

"I'll take full responsibility. Promise," Phainon reassured, giving his hands a quick squeeze. 

"...Okay," he swallowed. "I haven't always been good at saying things out loud. Talking about feelings the way you do doesn’t come as easy to me. But there’s one thing I've always known and didn't need words to understand is that... I've always wanted a piece of you. Even when you weren't here. I knew it would be hard taking care of a baby on my own, but I… I wanted her so badly because she was a piece of you that I could call mine. That I would always know that if you didn’t come back, I’d always have her. But now you are, and I've realized that what I want most in life—is one with you. Even if we argue. Even if we fight. Because I know you're obsessed with me just enough to forgive me every time," Mydei added lightly. 

Phainon snorted a little at that.

"But from the moment you came back into my... our lives, I promised myself that I'd try. That even if I didn't have the right words, I'd try to show you in other ways. In the ways I touched you and in the way I did things I'd do for you." Mydei continued, "Truth be told, I don't know how to want anyone else, and not because I can't, but because you're all I've ever needed."

Phainon didn't move at first. Mydei closed his eyes, already feeling the pinpricks of heat spread across his face. 

God, this was so embarrassing. 

He felt Phainon let go of one of his hands. Mydei cracked one eye open just in time for Phainon to reach up to wipe a stray tear from the corner of Mydei's eye. 

"That was–”

"Stupid," Mydei offered, blushing furiously. 

"No," Phainon's voice was firm. "I was going to say perfect. You don't have to say it all in words... I know you love me. Otherwise I would've gotten the boot long ago for talking about another baby."

"Here we go again," Mydei playfully rolled his eyes before turning to lie back on his pillow, pulling the sheets snug around him. "Goodnight, Phainon."

Phainon let out a small whine, flopping onto his side of the bed. He came up behind Mydei, arms wrapping around him as he rested his chin on his bicep. 

"Would it really be so bad?"

"Crying, diaper changes, not getting any sleep, and not to mention all the pregnancy symptoms," Mydei rattled off the top of his head, glancing back at his very needy fiancé. "Shall I go on?"

"But Augusta would have a sibling. We'd get to turn the extra room into a nursery, pick out little clothes..." Phainon trailed off. 

Mydei sighed. "You're serious about this, I take it?"

"Pretty sure I've been serious, sweetheart."

Then Phainon's eyes widened. 

"Is that... Mydei, is that really a yes?" 

Mydei just turned his back to him, tugging the blanket higher once again, failing to hide the smile tugging at his lips. Even through the morning sickness and eventual late-night feedings, he’d do it all over again with Phainon. But still, he liked keeping him on his toes.

"'Night, Phainon."

The walk back from Phainon's parents house was peaceful. The sun was dipping just below the horizon as the three of them made their way home for dinner. The walk home wasn't far, which was something they had both been grateful for, especially since it meant that Audata and Heironymus could look after Augusta when things got too busy or they just needed some... alone time. It had been nice for Phainon too. Having his parents closer, a recent change from their old house in the suburbs

Mydei hadn’t been feeling well. When Audata had insisted that they stay for dinner, Mydei had politely declined, promising that they'd be back another day, and chalking up the ache in his back to stress instead of admitting the truth. 

He knew Phainon had been a little disappointed, he'd been looking forward to his mother's cooking. Mydei had told him to stay, but Phainon didn't want him to head home alone. 

Now, they were walking side by side. The ache had only intensified, but Phainon still had enough energy for the both of them. 

And so did Augusta. 

The little girl was already a few paces ahead of them, skipping along the sidewalk, still in view. 

"Not too far!" Phainon called out. 

Augusta stopped. "I know papa!" she called back. 

Mydei smiled a little as Phainon hooked their arms together. 

"...So did you not want to deal with my mother?"

"I like your mother."

"Doesn't answer the question," Phainon hummed, but he dropped the topic. "Well, you barely ate yesterday, so I know something is up. Anything you want for dinner then? Maybe stew or rice, you liked that last time with the side salad--"

"You're going to overdo it again," Mydei sighed. 

"I'm not."

"You say that and then we end up with enough food to feed eight people."

Phainon pouted, letting out a soft "hmph". "I don't hear you complaining when you're eating it."

Mydei playfully rolled his eyes, keeping his gaze forward on Augusta. He watched as she stopped near a flowerbed, crouching down to inspect some of the petals. His hand drifted over his stomach unconsciously. 

"I don't think the baby's been agreeing with most things lately," he said without so much so  as a second thought. 

"Then maybe a light soup or..." Phainon stopped dead in his tracks, jerking Mydei back from the suddenness of it. 

"What?"

"Babe... what did you just say?"

"Huh?"

"You said the baby hasn't been agreeing lately. Are you the baby?"

"Oh."

"Oh? is that all you have to say for yourself?"

Mydei took a breath, taking Phainon's hand and placing it on his stomach. "I'm pregnant."

"You better not be messing with me. You know my heart is fragile," his voice was already breaking around the edges.

Mydei laughed. "I'm not messing with you. I'm really pregnant, but this wasn’t how I wanted you to find out."

"When did you...find out?"

"A week ago. Six weeks along."

Phainon sputtered, clearly stunned. "A week?! And you didn't tell me?!"

Mydei shrugged. "You were getting under my skin."

Phainon narrowed his eyes in response, but then he relaxed his shoulders, face breaking out into a wide grin as he hooked one arm around Mydei's waist. He pulled him into a tight hug, almost lifting him off the ground. 

"We're really having a baby,” his voice was barely above a whisper

"Yeah," Mydei nodded with a quiet laugh. 

Phainon set him down on his feet. He leaned in, tilting his face as Mydei planted a hand on his chest, letting their lips meet in a sweet kiss. His hand came up to Mydei's waist, pulling him closer to deepen the kiss. Mydei practically melted against him when Phainon nipped lightly at his bottom lip, a soft groan escaping him despite himself. 

"Ew! Mama, Papa!" Augusta's voice rang out. They pulled apart, a little breathless to see her in the distance. She was facing them with her hands on her hips. "Stop kissing! You're taking so long!" 

Phainon cleared his throat. "We're coming!" he called back, cupping his hands around his mouth.

He turned toward Mydei, offering his arm again. Mydei hooked his arm through his so they could catch up to their daughter again. 

Phainon let out a wistful sigh. "God.. I know I've been wanting this, but I didn't think it'd happen so soon... and so close to the wedding."

"Oh God," Mydei groaned. "We are not telling Cipher until after the wedding. She'll never let me live this down."
